title: Context Windows and API Cost: What You Actually Pay
description: Separate a model's maximum context capacity from the number of tokens you send and pay for.
tldr: A 200,000-token context window is a capacity limit, not a flat charge. You pay for tokens actually processed, subject to the model's billing rules and any long-context price tiers.

sections.heading: Capacity is not usage
sections.body: A context window caps the material the model can consider in one request. Selecting a model with a 200K window does not mean every request bills 200K tokens. A 2K-token prompt is billed based on its actual input usage, even if the model could accept much more.

sections.heading: History makes later turns larger
sections.body: In a chat app, prior messages may be resent on every turn. A conversation that begins with a small prompt can become expensive because the input grows. Log input tokens by turn and set policies for summarizing, trimming or retrieving only relevant history.

sections.heading: Long input can change the rate
sections.body: Some provider price sheets distinguish requests above a context threshold or specify different rates for particular model modes. Before estimating a 100K-token document, inspect the exact model's current pricing notes, not just the headline input rate. Output, cache reads and non-text inputs may also have separate prices.

sections.heading: A 100K-token document example
sections.body: At an illustrative $3 per million input tokens, 100,000 input tokens would cost $0.30 before output. If the model returned 2,000 tokens at $15 per million, output would add $0.03. Repeating the full document across 1,000 requests would cost about $330 at those sample rates. Retrieval or caching may change that economics.

sections.heading: Design around the task
sections.body: Measure answer quality with a short relevant excerpt versus the full document. If retrieval meets your quality target, it reduces billable input. If the task requires global reasoning across the entire file, a long context model may be justified. [Compare model prices](/tools/compare-prices) using your actual token mix.

faq.question: Does a large context window cost money by itself?
faq.answer: No. You pay for actual usage and any model-specific billing categories, not the unused capacity.

ctaText: Use the TokenRate tools to calculate cost from your own usage and the current model rates.
